information.status:
Linux application server: HTTPS is reachable from the application gateway; SSH and monitoring are reachable only from their approved management sources.
The front and rear rack doors latch, and the sampled asset labels match the rack elevation record.
information.inspectionDetails:
SCOPE
Fictional evidence snapshot for the inspected rack, collected during the current assessment shift. Host: app-01, 10.40.20.21; management address: 10.40.10.21. Source: authenticated host inventory, service configuration, firewall rules, and approved connectivity tests.

LISTENERS AND PROCESS OWNERS
TCP 10.40.20.21:443 | nginx | HTTPS application endpoint.
TCP 10.40.10.21:22 | sshd | Administrative SSH.
TCP 10.40.10.21:9100 | node_exporter | Host metrics.
TCP 127.0.0.1:8080 | java | Application backend; loopback only.

REACHABILITY AND CONFIGURATION
Application gateway 10.40.20.10 reaches 443; user VLAN tests cannot reach 22 or 9100.
Only bastion 10.40.10.10 reaches SSH. Named administrators use individual SSH certificates; direct root login and password login are disabled. Bastion sign-in records show MFA.
Only monitoring collector 10.40.10.15 reaches 9100. The backend is not directly reachable from another host.
TLS configuration permits 1.2/1.3 with the approved cipher profile; the certificate matches the service name and is within validity.
The latest maintenance record shows the approved patch baseline; central logging and endpoint-agent heartbeats are current.
No additional TCP listeners appear in the host inventory. This is a point-in-time observation, not proof that all vulnerabilities are absent.
information.nistControl:
CM-6 Configuration Settings; CM-7 Least Functionality
AC-17 Remote Access; SC-7 Boundary Protection
IA-2 Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users)
information.riskGuidance:
Compare each listener with the server role and approved source networks.
SSH and metrics ports are expected here because access restrictions and ownership are evidenced. Consider application compromise separately from management-plane exposure; a port list alone does not establish either vulnerability or compliance.

information.status:
Windows management server: RDP and remote administration are limited to the approved bastion and automation host.
Administrative identities are individual, and the emergency local account is controlled through the credential vault.
information.inspectionDetails:
SCOPE
Host: win-mgmt-01, 10.40.10.31. Evidence: local listener export, Windows service-to-process mapping, effective firewall policy, and sign-in records.

LISTENERS AND SERVICE MAPPING
TCP/UDP 3389 | Remote Desktop Services (TermService; service-host process) | Remote administration.
TCP 5986 | WinRM HTTPS listener; HTTP.sys handles the listener | Approved automation.
TCP 135 and assigned dynamic RPC ports | RPC endpoint mapper and registered Windows services | Restricted domain-management functions.
TCP 445 | Server service/SMB, kernel networking | Approved administrative file transfer.
Process IDs are intentionally omitted: they change after restart. Service ownership was verified locally, not guessed from port numbers.

CONTROL EVIDENCE
The user and guest VLAN test hosts cannot reach these listeners. RDP is permitted only from bastion 10.40.10.10; WinRM only from automation host 10.40.10.12.
SMB/RPC rules allow only the documented domain-management peers. Network Level Authentication is enabled for RDP; it is not itself MFA.
MFA is enforced at the remote-access entry point; sampled sessions map to named privileged accounts.
The WinRM HTTPS certificate matches the management name. The emergency local password is unique, vault-managed, and access-audited.
Recent event forwarding and endpoint-protection heartbeats are present. The patch report is within the site's approved maintenance window.
information.nistControl:
AC-2 Account Management; AC-17 Remote Access
IA-2 Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users)
CM-6 Configuration Settings; SC-7 Boundary Protection
information.riskGuidance:
RDP, SMB, and RPC are not automatic findings when required by the host role and restricted to approved peers.
Assess whether an ordinary user or compromised workstation can reach privileged services, whether access is attributable, and whether emergency credentials are managed.

information.status:
Out-of-band controller: the management interface is on a dedicated network and is inaccessible from application and user VLANs.
Remote console access is attributable to named operators; unused controller protocols are disabled.
information.inspectionDetails:
SCOPE
Embedded controller: bmc-01, 10.40.99.21. This is a separate device from the server operating system; OS process listings do not describe its firmware services.

CONTROLLER SERVICE INVENTORY
TCP 443 | Embedded HTTPS management and Redfish API | Enabled.
UDP 161 | Embedded SNMP agent | SNMPv3 authentication/privacy enabled; collector-only access.
TCP 22 | Controller SSH | Disabled under this site's baseline.
UDP 623 | IPMI over LAN/RMCP+ | Disabled under this site's baseline.

CORROBORATING EVIDENCE
Service identity is confirmed by controller configuration export and authenticated API response, not port assignment alone.
Only the management bastion reaches 443; only the monitoring collector reaches 161. Test traffic from user and application VLANs is denied by the management firewall.
Controller access uses approved named identities. Emergency access is vaulted; the commissioning account is disabled.
Firmware inventory matches the approved version for this hardware model, with no overdue advisory remediation in the maintenance tracker.
Remote-console and virtual-media events are forwarded to central logging. Unused virtual-media access is disabled.
The management patch cable terminates in the documented out-of-band switch port; the rack key-control register is current.
information.nistControl:
CM-6 Configuration Settings; CM-7 Least Functionality
AC-2 Account Management; SC-7 Boundary Protection
AU-12 Audit Record Generation
information.riskGuidance:
Out-of-band access may permit power control, remote console use, and boot-media changes even when the operating system is unavailable.
Evaluate management-network isolation, credential handling, and firmware maintenance independently of the OS patch report. SNMPv3 being enabled does not prove that older SNMP versions are disabled; the configuration export must establish both.

information.status:
Storage server: file services are restricted to the documented application clients.
The export rules and local configuration match the approved storage role, and a recent sample restore is recorded.
information.inspectionDetails:
SCOPE
Storage host: store-01, data address 10.40.30.41 and management address 10.40.10.41. Evidence: authenticated configuration export, host inventory, client allowlist, and restore record.

SERVICE INVENTORY
TCP 10.40.30.41:2049 | Kernel NFS service (nfsd workers) | NFSv4-only data service.
TCP 10.40.10.41:22 | sshd | Management through the bastion.
TCP 10.40.10.41:9100 | node_exporter | Monitoring collector only.
No NFSv3/rpcbind service is enabled in the inspected configuration.

ACCESS AND RECOVERY EVIDENCE
Only application clients 10.40.20.21 and 10.40.20.22 are allowed through the storage firewall.
The inspected export uses Kerberos privacy protection and root squashing; its client scope is explicit rather than wildcard.
A test from the user VLAN cannot reach the NFS listener. A test identity without the required file permissions is denied.
Backup policy covers the exported data. The most recent completed restore test opened a sampled recovered file and recorded the comparison result.
Drive serials and bay labels match the hardware inventory. There are no unattended removed drives on the rack shelf.
Backup existence alone would not prove recoverability; the restore result is separate evidence.
information.nistControl:
AC-3 Access Enforcement; SC-7 Boundary Protection
CM-6 Configuration Settings
CP-9 System Backup; CP-10 System Recovery and Reconstitution
information.riskGuidance:
Assess unauthorized data access and modification against the export's sensitivity and client trust boundaries.
Separate access controls, transport protection, backups, and demonstrated restoration: each addresses a different failure mode.

information.status:
Database server: the database listener is restricted to its application tier, and administrative access uses the management network.
No development web interface or ad hoc file-sharing process appears in the listener inventory.
information.inspectionDetails:
SCOPE
Host: db-01, data address 10.40.30.51 and management address 10.40.10.51. Evidence: authenticated process inventory, PostgreSQL configuration, effective network rules, and log sample.

LISTENERS AND PROCESSES
TCP 10.40.30.51:5432 | postgres | Application database.
TCP 10.40.10.51:22 | sshd | Named administrators via the bastion.
TCP 10.40.10.51:9187 | postgres_exporter | Monitoring collector only.
PostgreSQL runs as its dedicated unprivileged service identity.

CONTROL EVIDENCE
Only the two approved application hosts can reach 5432; user VLAN traffic is denied.
The applicable host-based authentication rule requires TLS and SCRAM authentication. No matching trust rule exists for network clients.
The application role has the documented database privileges and no superuser privilege. Administrative roles are separate from application credentials.
The monitoring endpoint is denied from the application and user VLANs.
Sampled authentication failures and administrative changes appear in the central log store. The current backup job and a separate restoration check have completed successfully.
The service inventory is reconciled to the approved database role; no unsupported version claim is inferred from a remote banner.
information.nistControl:
AC-3 Access Enforcement; AC-6 Least Privilege
CM-6 Configuration Settings; SC-7 Boundary Protection
AU-12 Audit Record Generation; CP-9 System Backup
information.riskGuidance:
An open database port is expected for an application database. Evaluate its permitted clients, authentication rules, service-account privileges, and the sensitivity of stored data.
A private IP address alone is not a control; verify actual network and database enforcement.

information.status:
Rack physical inspection: doors, blanking panels, cable routing, and power-feed labels match the approved installation record.
Sampled management services are restricted to their documented networks, and no temporary service is listed.
information.inspectionDetails:
PHYSICAL WALKDOWN
Front and rear doors are closed and latched; no keys are left in the locks. Access authorization is recorded in the rack key register.
The sampled asset tags, serial numbers, and installed rack-unit positions match the inventory. No unrecorded device is connected.
Unused rack openings have blanking panels; intake and exhaust paths are unobstructed. Cables are supported without visible damage or pressure against fan outlets.
Each sampled dual-supply server has one cable to PDU A and one to PDU B. The electrician-approved circuit schedule traces them to separate UPS distribution paths. Cable color alone was not used as proof of independence.
PDU readings are below the site-documented operating limit for the circuits; no load limit is inferred from breaker labels alone.
The rack inlet sensor reads 23 C; the local approved operating band is 18-27 C. A second probe is within the sensor tolerance specified in the maintenance record.

NETWORK SAMPLE
BMC 10.40.99.21: TCP 443, embedded controller HTTPS; bastion-only.
OS 10.40.10.21: TCP 22, sshd; bastion-only.
OS 10.40.10.21: TCP 9100, node_exporter; collector-only.
Listener ownership is confirmed by authenticated inventory. The sample does not represent a complete inventory of every machine in the rack.
information.nistControl:
PE-3 Physical Access Control; PE-9 Power Equipment and Cabling
PE-11 Emergency Power; PE-14 Environmental Controls
CM-8 System Component Inventory
information.riskGuidance:
Consider physical tampering, loss of power redundancy, and cooling impairment separately.
Trace redundant power to upstream distribution rather than assuming two cords mean two independent supplies. Use the site's approved environmental limits for the installed equipment.

anomalies.status:
Linux server: SSH and a temporary file-sharing process are reachable from the general user VLAN, contrary to the approved management-only rule.
The temporary service exposes a deployment directory containing configuration backups.
anomalies.inspectionDetails:
SCOPE
Host: app-01, 10.40.20.21. Evidence: authenticated listener/process export, process launch record, effective firewall policy, and a limited approved reachability check.

OBSERVED LISTENERS
TCP 0.0.0.0:22 | sshd | Password authentication and direct root login enabled.
TCP 0.0.0.0:443 | nginx | Expected application service.
TCP 0.0.0.0:8000 | python3 | Temporary HTTP file service running as the deployment account.
TCP 127.0.0.1:8080 | java | Application backend.
A wildcard bind describes local interfaces; the separate connectivity test below establishes remote exposure.

CORROBORATING EVIDENCE
The approved role permits HTTPS from the application gateway and SSH from the bastion only. It lists no port-8000 service.
The user VLAN test host completes connections to 22 and 8000. The effective host firewall rule permits both from the user subnet.
The process working directory is a deployment backup folder. An approved metadata-only check sees a directory index containing configuration-backup filenames; file contents and credentials were not collected.
The service launch record has no matching approved change ticket. No process exploit or credential guessing was performed.
The configuration backup inventory identifies the folder as containing secrets that should be vault-managed.
anomalies.nistControl:
CM-7 Least Functionality; CM-6 Configuration Settings
AC-6 Least Privilege; AC-17 Remote Access
SC-7 Boundary Protection
anomalies.riskGuidance:
The finding is the unapproved service and demonstrated access path, not merely the presence of SSH or HTTP.
Consider exposure of deployment secrets, privileged remote access, and lateral movement from a compromised user endpoint. Prioritize removing unintended access while preserving evidence and following change procedures.

anomalies.status:
Windows server: ordinary user workstations can reach administrative services outside the approved access path.
A shared local administrator identity is used for RDP, and no current credential-rotation record is available.
anomalies.inspectionDetails:
SCOPE
Host: win-mgmt-01, 10.40.10.31. Evidence: local listener/service inventory, effective firewall export, account configuration, and sampled sign-in records.

LISTENERS
TCP/UDP 3389 | Remote Desktop Services | Reachable from the user VLAN.
TCP 5985 | WinRM over HTTP transport | Reachable from the user VLAN.
TCP 445 | SMB/Server service | Reachable from the user VLAN.
TCP 135 and dynamic RPC listeners | Windows RPC services | Present in local inventory; not exhaustively tested remotely.

POLICY AND OBSERVATIONS
The site's approved rule restricts administration to the bastion and automation subnet. The active firewall group permits the entire internal network instead.
RDP Network Level Authentication is disabled. Sampled successful RDP events use the same local support-admin account across two operator shifts.
The account is privileged; its owner and current unique-password rotation record cannot be established from the credential register.
The WinRM configuration explicitly enables Basic authentication and AllowUnencrypted. An export confirms no HTTPS listener. No credential capture was performed.
HTTP transport on port 5985 alone would not prove cleartext remoting: authentication and message-protection settings must also be inspected.
No approved exception covers these differences from the baseline.
anomalies.nistControl:
AC-2 Account Management; AC-17 Remote Access
IA-5 Authenticator Management; CM-6 Configuration Settings
SC-7 Boundary Protection; SC-8 Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity
anomalies.riskGuidance:
Assess credential exposure and administrative access from a compromised user machine.
Shared identities also weaken attribution. Distinguish confirmed configuration weaknesses from an unproven compromise; successful logins are not automatically evidence of an intruder.

anomalies.status:
Out-of-band controller: a cabling and network-rule mismatch exposes the controller to the user VLAN.
An unchanged commissioning credential remains active, and SNMPv2c is enabled outside the approved monitoring configuration.
anomalies.inspectionDetails:
SCOPE
Controller: bmc-01, 10.40.99.21. Evidence: switch-port mapping, controller configuration, commissioning checklist, and approved connectivity tests. This is not an OS process scan.

CONTROLLER SERVICES
TCP 443 | Embedded HTTPS console/Redfish | Reachable from the user VLAN.
TCP 22 | Embedded SSH service | Enabled and reachable from the user VLAN.
UDP 161 | Embedded SNMP agent | SNMPv2c configuration enabled; the recorded community is the vendor example value.
UDP 623 | IPMI over LAN/RMCP+ | Enabled in the controller configuration. UDP reachability has not been conclusively established.

CORROBORATING EVIDENCE
The management cable is patched to a production switch access port instead of the documented isolated management port. The active network rule permits user-to-controller traffic.
The provisioning checklist marks credential rotation incomplete, and the authorized owner confirms the commissioning credential remains unchanged. No passwords are included in this evidence.
A read-only controller audit shows a privileged commissioning account still enabled. No approved exception authorizes its retention.
The firmware review task is overdue, but this snapshot does not claim a specific exploitable CVE without a model/version advisory match.
The site baseline calls for isolated HTTPS management, named access, and SNMPv3-only monitoring.
anomalies.nistControl:
SC-7 Boundary Protection; IA-5 Authenticator Management
AC-2 Account Management; CM-6 Configuration Settings
SI-2 Flaw Remediation
anomalies.riskGuidance:
Controller compromise can affect power state, console access, and boot configuration independently of OS protections.
Prioritize the confirmed reachability and credential failures. Do not interpret an ambiguous UDP result as proof that a service is closed or safe.

anomalies.status:
Storage server: an NFS export is available to the general user subnet and grants writable access beyond the approved application clients.
The effective export rule also disables root squashing.
anomalies.inspectionDetails:
SCOPE
Host: store-01, 10.40.30.41. Evidence: authenticated export configuration, local service inventory, firewall rules, and approved access-test record.

SERVICE INVENTORY
TCP 2049 | Kernel NFS service | NFSv4 enabled.
TCP 22 | sshd | Bastion-only management.
TCP 9100 | node_exporter | Collector-only metrics.

EXPORT AND ACCESS EVIDENCE
The project-data export permits the broad 10.40.0.0/16 client range, including the general user VLAN. Its options include read-write access, AUTH_SYS, and no_root_squash.
The approved storage record permits only the two application hosts and requires stronger authenticated access. There is no approved exception.
A user VLAN test host can reach 2049. A supervised test using a designated disposable test directory confirmed unauthorized read/write access; no production data was changed.
The host firewall rule mirrors the overly broad export client range. SSH restrictions are correct and do not mitigate the data-service exposure.
The most recent backup completed, but it does not prevent unauthorized reading or alteration of the live export.
Evidence of exfiltration or previous tampering was not established by this inspection.
anomalies.nistControl:
AC-3 Access Enforcement; AC-6 Least Privilege
CM-6 Configuration Settings; SC-7 Boundary Protection
anomalies.riskGuidance:
Consider unauthorized disclosure and modification of shared data, including the effect of trusting client-supplied identities.
Assess export permissions and reachable clients together. The risk is not simply that port 2049 is open; it is that access exceeds the documented role and was demonstrated in a controlled test.

anomalies.status:
Database server: the management boundary permits general user access to PostgreSQL, and a matching host-authentication rule uses trust.
A metrics endpoint is also exposed outside its approved collector network.
anomalies.inspectionDetails:
SCOPE
Host: db-01, 10.40.30.51. Evidence: authenticated process inventory, database authentication-rule export, firewall policy, and a supervised test with a designated assessment identity.

LISTENERS AND PROCESSES
TCP 0.0.0.0:5432 | postgres | Database listener on all IPv4 interfaces.
TCP 0.0.0.0:9187 | postgres_exporter | Database metrics.
TCP 10.40.10.51:22 | sshd | Management listener.

CORROBORATING EVIDENCE
The firewall permits the user subnet to 5432 and 9187; approved policy permits application hosts and the monitoring collector respectively.
The first applicable PostgreSQL host-authentication rule for the user subnet uses trust. A supervised connection with the designated test database role succeeds without a password.
The test role is limited; this inspection did not attempt superuser access or enumerate production records. The rule's broad database/user match is confirmed by the configuration export.
An unauthenticated metrics response reveals database and instance labels from the user subnet. No vulnerability is inferred solely from the exporter process name.
The database backup is current, but backup status does not address this access-control failure.
anomalies.nistControl:
AC-3 Access Enforcement; IA-2 Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users)
CM-6 Configuration Settings; SC-7 Boundary Protection
anomalies.riskGuidance:
Evaluate access without authentication against the privileges of reachable database roles and data sensitivity.
Prioritize the database authentication and network-scope defects; exposed metrics may aid reconnaissance but should not be equated with proven access to all database contents.

anomalies.status:
Rack physical inspection: a rear door is held open by a cable bundle, and both power supplies on sampled dual-supply servers terminate on the same PDU.
The approved installation record requires a secured rack and separate A/B power distribution.
anomalies.inspectionDetails:
PHYSICAL EVIDENCE
The rear latch cannot engage because a temporary cable bundle passes through the door opening. No approved maintenance window or attendant is recorded.
Two sampled servers have both supply cords connected to PDU A. PDU B is present but unused for those servers. The circuit schedule confirms that loss of PDU A would remove both feeds.
A temporary unmanaged switch is connected on the rear shelf; its serial number is absent from the current asset record and no installation ticket is available. No claim is made that it is malicious.
Several empty rack units lack blanking panels. The measured upper-front inlet is 31 C, above this site's posted 27 C upper operating threshold, with a 25-minute trend above threshold.

NETWORK SAMPLE
Controller: TCP 443, embedded HTTPS, management-only.
OS: TCP 22, sshd, bastion-only; TCP 443, nginx, application-gateway-only.
The sampled listener restrictions match policy. These passing checks do not resolve the separate physical and availability findings.
No power interruption or intrusive cable tracing was performed during the assessment.
anomalies.nistControl:
PE-3 Physical Access Control; PE-9 Power Equipment and Cabling
PE-11 Emergency Power; PE-14 Environmental Controls
CM-8 System Component Inventory
anomalies.riskGuidance:
Consider unauthorized physical access, a common power failure point, and equipment overheating.
Corroborate the unrecorded switch's owner and network role before classifying intent. Coordinate remediation with operations rather than unplugging live equipment during an inspection.

information.status:
The controlled door closes fully and the latch engages after the authorized entry cycle.
Badge decisions and door-position events appear in the access log with consistent timestamps.
information.inspectionDetails:
WALKDOWN
Reader housing is secured, with no loose cover or exposed terminals. The strike and latch align; the door is not obstructed.
A supervised test badge assigned to the room is accepted. A designated unassigned test badge is rejected. No tailgating test was performed.
The door returns to its secured state after the normal release interval. The door-position display agrees with the observed position.

RECORD SAMPLE
The test access decision, door-open event, and door-close event appear under the expected reader ID.
The sampled terminated worker's badge is disabled in the current authorization list.
The current shift's review record includes follow-up for the previous shift's held-open alert.
Emergency egress arrangements are documented separately; these entry tests do not establish life-safety compliance.
information.nistControl:
PE-2 Physical Access Authorizations; PE-3 Physical Access Control
PE-6 Monitoring Physical Access; AU-6 Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
information.riskGuidance:
Evaluate whether entry is limited to authorized people and abnormal door states are detected and reviewed.
A functioning reader alone does not prove that the door secures or that badge authorizations are current.

information.status:
The reader and door hardware are intact, and the security desk receives the supervised held-open alert.
The door relatches when released; no persistent bypass is configured.
information.inspectionDetails:
PHYSICAL CHECK
No wedge, tape, or improvised tie is holding the door. The latch returns freely and the reader cable enters through protected conduit.
The approved maintenance inspection records current door closer and strike checks.

SUPERVISED FUNCTION TEST
An authorized badge releases the door for the normal entry interval. The door closes and secures afterward.
During a planned held-open test, the security desk receives the correct door identifier and acknowledges the event. Normal state returns after closure.
The panel and central console timestamps agree within the site's documented event-correlation tolerance.
The test record identifies the operator, the security-desk acknowledgement, and restoration to normal operation.
A fault test is not evidence of an ongoing fault when the system detects it and is restored as documented.
information.nistControl:
PE-3 Physical Access Control; PE-6 Monitoring Physical Access
AU-8 Time Stamps; MA-2 Controlled Maintenance
information.riskGuidance:
Check detection, response, and restoration as well as mechanical closure.
Assess whether an abnormal door state would persist unnoticed and whether logs can be correlated with nearby camera evidence.

anomalies.status:
The door is held open and will not return to its secured state.
The security desk has no acknowledgement for the sustained held-open condition.
anomalies.inspectionDetails:
PHYSICAL EVIDENCE
A temporary cable protector prevents full closure. The latch remains clear of the strike and the door cannot be secured without addressing the obstruction.
The reader still records accepted badges, which does not prevent someone from entering through the open doorway.

CORROBORATING RECORDS
The door-position input reports open continuously through the previous two patrol samples.
The console shows a held-open condition but no acknowledgement or approved maintenance exception.
The maintenance ticket for the temporary cable route has no assigned restoration time.
The posted room rule requires the door to remain secured outside supervised entry.
This finding concerns loss of controlled entry; it does not assume a particular person entered without authorization.
anomalies.nistControl:
PE-3 Physical Access Control; PE-6 Monitoring Physical Access
AU-6 Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
anomalies.riskGuidance:
Consider the exposure window, accessible equipment, and whether other barriers or staffed monitoring compensate.
A working badge reader does not mitigate a doorway that remains physically open.

anomalies.status:
The door remains unlocked after the normal badge-release interval.
The panel configuration shows a maintenance unlock override with no current authorization.
anomalies.inspectionDetails:
FUNCTIONAL EVIDENCE
The door closes, but the entry-side handle continues to release it without presenting a badge. A supervised test confirms this after the normal access interval has expired.
The reader accepts the designated test badge and logs the event, but badge acceptance is not required to reopen the door.

CONFIGURATION AND RECORD REVIEW
The controller status shows a persistent unlock override.
The maintenance work order that originally requested the override is marked complete; no follow-up record authorizes leaving it enabled.
The panel state is inconsistent with the posted secured-room operating rule.
Door-position events are being logged, so the defect is not explained by a missing door sensor.
The assessment does not alter emergency-egress hardware or power-loss behavior.
anomalies.nistControl:
PE-3 Physical Access Control; CM-6 Configuration Settings
MA-2 Controlled Maintenance; PE-6 Monitoring Physical Access
anomalies.riskGuidance:
Assess entry without authorization despite apparently normal reader operation.
Investigate the duration of the override and review relevant access/camera records; absence of a badge event cannot prove nobody entered through an unlocked door.

information.status:
The stored-pressure extinguisher is visible and accessible at its marked location.
The pin and tamper seal are intact, the gauge is in its marked operating range, and the inspection record is current.
information.inspectionDetails:
VISUAL OBSERVATIONS
The extinguisher is secured in its bracket; the route to it is unobstructed by boxes or equipment.
The operating label is legible. The cylinder has no visible severe corrosion, denting, or leakage, and the hose/nozzle is unobstructed.
This unit has a pressure gauge; its needle is within the manufacturer's marked operating range. The pin and tamper seal are present.

RECORD CHECK
The unit identifier matches the inspection register. The monthly visual check and annual maintenance record are current relative to the assessment date.
The equipment schedule identifies this extinguisher type for the local hazard assessment.
This visual check does not establish internal condition or substitute for servicing, and the unit was not discharged during inspection.
information.nistControl: PE-13 Fire Protection; MA-2 Controlled Maintenance
information.riskGuidance:
Consider timely access to a suitable, maintained extinguisher under the facility's emergency plan.
A green gauge alone is insufficient: location, condition, hazard suitability, and records also matter.

information.status:
The CO2 extinguisher is accessible, with an intact pin and seal and a current maintenance record.
Its service record documents the required weight check; the unit has no pressure gauge by design.
information.inspectionDetails:
VISUAL OBSERVATIONS
The CO2 unit is in its designated bracket, and the horn and hose have no visible obstruction or damage.
The operating instructions and unit identifier are legible. The access path is clear.
No pressure gauge is fitted; absence of a gauge on this model is not a defect.

RECORD CHECK
The maintenance sheet identifies the unit by serial number and records its weight check against the manufacturer's specified charged weight and tolerance.
The most recent visual check and maintenance due date are current. The service register shows no overdue applicable cylinder test.
The facility hazard assessment and emergency plan document this unit's placement.
The assessor reviewed records and external condition only; charge adequacy was not inferred from appearance.
information.nistControl: PE-13 Fire Protection; MA-2 Controlled Maintenance
information.riskGuidance:
Apply model-appropriate inspection criteria.
Evaluate whether the available evidence supports readiness; do not classify a CO2 unit as defective simply because it lacks a gauge.

anomalies.status:
The extinguisher cannot be reached without moving stacked shipping cartons.
The location's latest scheduled visual inspection is overdue, with no documented substitute check.
anomalies.inspectionDetails:
PHYSICAL EVIDENCE
Cartons extend across the direct access path and conceal the lower part of the extinguisher cabinet. The cabinet cannot fully open while the cartons remain.
The location sign is visible, but the unit itself is not immediately accessible.

RECORD EVIDENCE
The inspection register identifies this exact unit and shows that the latest monthly check was missed.
No electronic inspection entry or temporary relocation record closes the gap.
The annual service record remains current; that does not resolve the current obstruction or missed visual check.
The equipment was not moved or discharged by the assessor. The finding was communicated to the responsible facilities contact.
anomalies.nistControl: PE-13 Fire Protection; MA-2 Controlled Maintenance
anomalies.riskGuidance:
Consider the delay to an authorized emergency response and the possibility that a missed inspection allows a defect to persist.
Distinguish current accessibility from service history; one can fail while the other is satisfactory.

anomalies.status:
The stored-pressure unit's gauge is below its marked operating range and its tamper seal is broken.
No replacement unit or completed service record is documented for the location.
anomalies.inspectionDetails:
VISUAL EVIDENCE
The gauge needle is below the manufacturer's marked operating band. The pin is present but the tamper seal is broken.
The hose appears externally intact; the label is legible and the access route is clear.

RECORD REVIEW
The defect was reported on the previous shift, but the maintenance ticket remains open.
The unit remains listed as available, and there is no record of a suitable temporary replacement.
A broken seal alone would require investigation rather than prove discharge; the low gauge reading provides additional evidence that this stored-pressure model may not be ready.
The assessor did not test-discharge or attempt to recharge the unit.
anomalies.nistControl: PE-13 Fire Protection; MA-2 Controlled Maintenance
anomalies.riskGuidance:
Assess reduced firefighting readiness for the location and how the facility's emergency arrangements cover the unavailable unit.
Have qualified personnel evaluate the defect; visual evidence cannot determine the remaining usable extinguishing capacity.

information.status:
The media-disposal container is locked, and the sampled drives are individually recorded in the custody manifest.
The batch is awaiting approved sanitization and has not been released to ordinary waste collection.
information.inspectionDetails:
PHYSICAL CHECK
The dedicated media container is in the controlled service area; its lid and lock are intact. No loose drive or tape is visible outside it.
The batch label matches the pending-sanitization register. Access is limited to the documented custodians.

CUSTODY SAMPLE
Under custodian supervision, two sampled serial numbers match the manifest, transfer signatures, and source-system retirement records.
The scheduled provider and proposed treatment are recorded for the relevant media types and information sensitivity.
A custody receipt is present; it is not presented as a sanitization certificate.
The batch remains in secure storage until treatment and verification records are accepted.
Labels are retained for traceability; having labels on securely controlled retired media is not itself a security failure.
information.nistControl:
MP-4 Media Storage; MP-5 Media Transport
MP-6 Media Sanitization
information.riskGuidance:
Assess loss or substitution of unsanitized media before treatment.
Check custody, physical protection, and the selected sanitization process separately; a locked container does not itself sanitize its contents.

information.status:
The disposal batch has completed the approved sanitization workflow, and its release record is reconciled to the asset manifest.
No unexplained extra media is present in the inspected container.
information.inspectionDetails:
RECORD SAMPLE
The release packet lists media identifiers, treatment method, operator, completion record, and verification/validation outcome for the sampled items.
The approved method is tied to the media type and information sensitivity rather than a universal number of overwrite passes.
Retirement records and custody transfers reconcile to the batch manifest; the receiving party and release authorization are recorded.

PHYSICAL SAMPLE
The container is secured pending collection. The batch identifier agrees with the release packet.
The sampled items correspond to the recorded disposition; no loose untracked drives are visible nearby.
A file deletion or ordinary format is not being used as the sole evidence of sanitization.
This is a sample-based records review; it does not claim a forensic examination of every device.
information.nistControl:
MP-6 Media Sanitization; MP-5 Media Transport
CM-8 System Component Inventory
information.riskGuidance:
Evaluate whether the disposition evidence is complete and appropriate to the media and data.
A generic destruction certificate without identifiers or custody linkage would not establish that the inspected batch was treated.

anomalies.status:
The media-disposal container is unlocked, with two retired drives outside the controlled custody record.
The pickup schedule places the container on the ordinary waste route before sanitization is documented.
anomalies.inspectionDetails:
PHYSICAL EVIDENCE
The lid is open and the lock is disengaged. Two drives are visible at the top of the container in an area accessible to delivery personnel.
The drives have source-system asset labels; those labels support traceability and are not the defect by themselves.

RECORD EVIDENCE
Neither sampled serial number appears on the active disposal manifest. No sanitization completion record is found for either item.
The collection sheet lists the general waste contractor, not the approved secure-media route.
The retirement record identifies the source systems as having held internal operational data. Contents were not read during the inspection.
The finding is an uncontrolled exposure opportunity, not proof that data has already been recovered by another person.
anomalies.nistControl:
MP-4 Media Storage; MP-5 Media Transport
MP-6 Media Sanitization; CM-8 System Component Inventory
anomalies.riskGuidance:
Consider unauthorized media removal and recoverable information, based on known source-system sensitivity.
Prioritize securing the batch and reconciling custody before release. Do not assume an unlabeled or visibly old drive contains no sensitive information.

anomalies.status:
The batch is marked ready for release, but its SSD treatment record documents only file deletion and a quick format.
The approval packet lacks a validated sanitization outcome for the sampled devices.
anomalies.inspectionDetails:
RECORD EVIDENCE
The batch manifest identifies solid-state drives and the retired systems that used them.
The work note records deleting user folders and quick-formatting the volumes. It does not identify an approved media sanitization procedure or its verification result.
The approval field is signed, but the required validation record is blank.
A contractor pickup is scheduled; custody controls remain intact until that point.

PHYSICAL SAMPLE
The locked container and serial-number labels match the manifest. These passing custody checks do not resolve the treatment gap.
The assessment did not attempt data recovery and does not claim that any particular file remains recoverable.
The selected method must account for the media technology and applicable policy; repeated generic overwrites are not assumed to sanitize every SSD storage location.
anomalies.nistControl: MP-6 Media Sanitization; MP-5 Media Transport
anomalies.riskGuidance:
Assess disclosure risk if inadequately sanitized devices leave organizational control.
The confirmed finding is unsupported sanitization approval; recoverability and sensitivity require separate evidence.

information.status:
The cooling unit's intake and discharge paths are clear, and the local sensor reading agrees with the independent probe.
The current-shift alarm test reached the designated facilities contact.
information.inspectionDetails:
PHYSICAL OBSERVATIONS
No cartons or cable coils obstruct the return-air grille. The service clearance marked on the floor is clear.
No visible condensate leak or standing water is present. The drain inspection record is current.
The unit has no displayed fan or filter fault.

MEASUREMENTS AND RECORDS
The monitored rack inlet is 23 C; a separate probe reads 23.4 C, within the site's documented sensor tolerance.
This scenario's approved inlet band is 18-27 C and its humidity band is 30-60% RH; the current humidity is 45% RH. These are local policy values for this exercise.
The 24-hour trend remains within those local limits. Alarm thresholds match the approved configuration.
A planned alarm test generated a facilities notification and acknowledgement; the controller was returned to normal.
The maintenance record identifies the unit and lists no overdue corrective action.
information.nistControl:
PE-14 Environmental Controls; MA-2 Controlled Maintenance
PE-15 Water Damage Protection
information.riskGuidance:
Evaluate environmental conditions at equipment inlets and alarm response, not just the cooling unit's setpoint.
A comfortable room reading does not rule out rack hot spots. Apply limits approved for the actual equipment and operating conditions.

information.status:
The cooling unit is operating without an active fault, and maintenance records show the standby unit and alarm path were tested.
No leak or airflow obstruction is visible in the inspected service area.
information.inspectionDetails:
WALKDOWN
Supply and return openings are unobstructed, service panels are secured, and the filter indicator is within its normal range.
Condensate piping has no visible leak; the nearby leak sensor is present and not covered by stored material.

OPERATING RECORDS
The unit controller reports normal fan operation. Current inlet readings are 22-24 C across the sampled rack positions.
The latest maintenance record includes the standby-unit functional test and return to normal configuration. No failover was forced during this assessment.
The facilities record shows a successful leak-sensor test and correct alarm identification at the monitoring console.
No maintenance bypass remains enabled. The trend and alarm history show no unresolved environmental excursion.
These records establish the sampled checks, not a full capacity study for the room.
information.nistControl:
PE-14 Environmental Controls; PE-15 Water Damage Protection
MA-2 Controlled Maintenance
information.riskGuidance:
Consider whether cooling loss or a water leak would be detected and whether documented backup capacity is available.
Distinguish a tested standby function from proof that the entire room meets its required resilience target.

anomalies.status:
The monitored rack inlet has exceeded the site's upper threshold, but temperature alarms remain in maintenance inhibit.
The maintenance window ended on the previous shift without a recorded restoration check.
anomalies.inspectionDetails:
MEASUREMENTS
The local inlet sensor reads 32 C and the independent probe reads 31.7 C. The approved local upper limit is 27 C.
The trend shows 38 continuous minutes above that limit; the assessment does not infer component damage from temperature alone.

CONFIGURATION AND RECORDS
The controller displays maintenance inhibit for high-temperature alarms. No facilities notification exists for the current excursion.
The work order says maintenance is complete, but its alarm-restoration step is unsigned.
Stored cartons partly obstruct the return grille. A causal link between that obstruction and the entire temperature excursion has not been established.
No approved exception permits operation above the documented limit or leaving the alarm inhibited.
The observation was escalated to the facilities operator; no live cooling settings were changed during inspection.
anomalies.nistControl:
PE-14 Environmental Controls; MA-2 Controlled Maintenance
CM-6 Configuration Settings
anomalies.riskGuidance:
Assess availability risk from sustained high inlet temperatures and delayed response due to suppressed alarms.
Separate measured threshold exceedance, confirmed alarm inhibition, and possible contributing airflow problems in the finding.

anomalies.status:
Water is visible below the cooling unit's condensate connection, and the nearby leak-sensor lead is disconnected.
An open maintenance ticket records the leak without a completed repair or temporary monitoring arrangement.
anomalies.inspectionDetails:
PHYSICAL EVIDENCE
A shallow wet area extends from the condensate connection toward the service-cable route. The source has not been opened or dismantled.
The leak-sensor cable is disconnected at its labeled connector; the controller reports a sensor fault.
No barrier or documented temporary observation routine is present.

RECORD SAMPLE
The maintenance ticket records the same location on the previous shift and remains open.
The central alarm history has a sensor-fault event but no acknowledgement or assigned responder.
Temperature is currently within the local operating band. A normal temperature reading does not resolve the water and detection defects.
The assessment records proximity to equipment; it does not claim that water has entered energized components.
anomalies.nistControl:
PE-15 Water Damage Protection; PE-14 Environmental Controls
MA-2 Controlled Maintenance
anomalies.riskGuidance:
Consider propagation to equipment, cables, and occupied work areas, together with delayed detection.
Have responsible facilities personnel evaluate the condition without disturbing energized equipment or assuming the visible leak is the only source.

information.status:
The camera view covers the assigned doorway and approach, and recorded playback is available for the required sample period.
The mount is secure and the lens is unobstructed.
information.inspectionDetails:
PHYSICAL AND IMAGE CHECK
No loose mounting fastener, lens obstruction, or damaged visible cable is observed.
The live view includes the approach and door threshold identified in the camera coverage plan.
A supervised walk-through produces usable images at the planned observation points under current lighting.

RECORDER CHECK
The recorder shows active recording. A sampled clip from the beginning of the site's 30-day retention requirement can be retrieved and played.
The 30-day duration is this scenario's local retention policy, not a universal NIST requirement.
The camera time agrees with the access-control event sample within the site's stated correlation tolerance.
The most recent low-light test has a passing recorded result; a daytime image alone would not establish night coverage.
Recorder access is restricted to the authorized security roles, and the sampled export event is attributable.
information.nistControl:
PE-6 Monitoring Physical Access; AU-11 Audit Record Retention
AU-8 Time Stamps; AC-3 Access Enforcement
information.riskGuidance:
Evaluate detection, usable recorded evidence, and authorized access to footage.
A live image does not establish recording, sufficient retention, night performance, or correct timestamps.

information.status:
The camera's assigned service-yard route is visible, and the sampled recording shows the required approach without an unexplained gap.
Monitoring records show a completed video-loss alert test.
information.inspectionDetails:
COVERAGE OBSERVATIONS
The image includes the gate approach and the marked media-collection route. The field of view matches the approved coverage drawing.
No parked object or foliage obstructs the sampled route during the inspection. The housing and cable entry are intact.

FUNCTIONAL RECORDS
A recorded clip, not just the live feed, shows the supervised walk-through at the expected time.
Playback remains available across the sampled start/end times of the retention interval specified by the local camera schedule.
The planned video-loss test produced the correct camera identifier at the security console and an acknowledgement.
The camera was restored after the test; no unresolved video-loss condition remains.
The coverage check does not claim facial identification at every distance or under untested weather conditions.
information.nistControl:
PE-6 Monitoring Physical Access; AU-11 Audit Record Retention
MA-2 Controlled Maintenance
information.riskGuidance:
Assess whether required activity is visible and retained at a quality adequate for the documented monitoring purpose.
Differentiate general observation from positive identification, and confirm fault response as well as normal operation.

anomalies.status:
The camera has shifted away from the assigned doorway, leaving the door threshold outside the recorded view.
A loose mount is visible and the repair ticket has no completion record.
anomalies.inspectionDetails:
PHYSICAL AND IMAGE EVIDENCE
The camera bracket is tilted relative to the installation reference photograph; one mounting point is visibly loose.
Both the live view and a sampled recorded clip omit the doorway threshold required by the coverage drawing.
A supervised walk-through at the threshold is not visible, although the adjacent corridor remains visible.

RECORD CHECK
The security log records a report of shifted alignment on the previous shift. The related repair ticket remains open.
Recording and timestamp checks pass for the area still in view; these do not compensate for the missing coverage.
There is no approved alternative camera covering the omitted threshold in the current coverage plan.
The inspection establishes a blind spot, not that unauthorized entry has occurred.
anomalies.nistControl: PE-6 Monitoring Physical Access; MA-2 Controlled Maintenance
anomalies.riskGuidance:
Consider unauthorized movement through the uncovered area and the loss of corroborating evidence for badge events.
Review any compensating patrol or camera coverage before estimating residual likelihood.

anomalies.status:
The live camera image is available, but recordings are overwritten after roughly one day.
The approved local schedule requires 30 days, and a requested older sample cannot be retrieved.
anomalies.inspectionDetails:
RECORDER EVIDENCE
The camera is online and its current view covers the assigned entrance.
The recorder storage policy for this channel is set to a one-day maximum age. This differs from the 30-day local retention requirement.
A clip from the previous seven-day review point is absent; the recorder reports it has expired rather than an access-denied error.

CORROBORATION
The channel's storage policy change has no corresponding approved exception.
The recorder clock is consistent with the current access-control sample, so a simple time-search mismatch does not explain the missing interval.
No alternate archive is listed for this channel. A successful live-view check had been recorded as the entire daily check.
The 30-day value is scenario policy; the defect is failure to meet that policy, not a universal retention minimum.
anomalies.nistControl:
AU-11 Audit Record Retention; PE-6 Monitoring Physical Access
CM-6 Configuration Settings
anomalies.riskGuidance:
Assess the effect on investigating incidents discovered after the short retention interval.
Separate the ability to observe an event now from the ability to reconstruct it later.

information.status:
The unattended security-desk workstation is locked, and visitor badges and physical keys are secured.
Current access reviews and shift-handover items are attributable to named operators.
information.inspectionDetails:
DESK WALKDOWN
The screen is locked when the operator leaves. The site's documented inactivity-lock setting is five minutes.
No password note or unrestricted visitor roster is visible from the public counter. Unissued badges and cabinet keys are in locked storage.
The screen is positioned away from the visitor waiting area.

RECORD SAMPLE
The visitor register records host, badge identifier, issue time, and return or expiry status for the sampled visits.
The prior shift's unreturned badge was disabled and recorded in the handover.
The operator signs in with an individual account and uses a separate authorized privilege elevation for access-rule changes.
The latest security handover lists open door alerts and responsible follow-up owners. No unresolved item is silently dropped from the handover.
information.nistControl:
AC-11 Device Lock; AC-2 Account Management; AC-6 Least Privilege
PE-2 Physical Access Authorizations; PE-8 Visitor Access Records
information.riskGuidance:
Assess whether an unattended desk permits badge creation, access-rule changes, or exposure of visitor information.
A staffed desk still needs controlled credentials, secure badge storage, and reliable handover records.

information.status:
The security workstation's badge-issuance function is limited to the operator's role, and a sampled visitor badge expires at the approved time.
No unattended administrative session is present.
information.inspectionDetails:
OBSERVATIONS
The operator authenticates with a named identity. The badge-printing interface requires the assigned issuance permission.
Blank cards are stored in a locked drawer; no master access card is left on the desk.
The public-facing counter does not expose the operator keyboard or an unlocked console.

RECORD CHECK
The sampled visitor record links a sponsor, an approved area, an expiration time, and a badge identifier.
The assigned access areas match the approved visit rather than all facility rooms.
A sampled expired test badge is shown disabled in the access system.
Badge issuance and modification logs identify the operator and change time.
The inspection sampled authorization records and a designated test badge; it did not disclose real visitor identities.
information.nistControl:
PE-2 Physical Access Authorizations; PE-3 Physical Access Control
PE-8 Visitor Access Records; AC-6 Least Privilege
AU-12 Audit Record Generation
information.riskGuidance:
Consider excessive or persistent visitor access and whether badge changes can be attributed.
Physical possession of a printed badge does not establish that its access scope or expiry is appropriate.

anomalies.status:
The security desk is unattended with an unlocked badge-administration session.
An unassigned privileged badge and a written credential note are accessible from the counter.
anomalies.inspectionDetails:
PHYSICAL OBSERVATIONS
The badge-administration interface remains open while the operator is absent. The session has access to badge activation controls.
An unassigned card identified in the issuance register as a privileged test badge is on the counter, not in locked storage.
A note labeled with the shared desk-account name and password is visible beside the keyboard; the credential value is not copied into this assessment.

CORROBORATING RECORDS
The automatic device-lock setting is disabled despite the site's five-minute requirement.
The desk session uses the shared operator account rather than an individual identity.
The shift log records no supervised maintenance exception for either condition.
No badge was created and no account was accessed by the assessor.
The finding concerns the opportunity for misuse and weak attribution, not evidence that misuse already happened.
anomalies.nistControl:
AC-11 Device Lock; IA-5 Authenticator Management
AC-2 Account Management; PE-3 Physical Access Control
anomalies.riskGuidance:
Assess unauthorized changes to physical access permissions and use of exposed credentials or badges.
The effect may extend beyond the workstation because its active session controls entry to other facility areas.

anomalies.status:
Visitor records show expired visits with badges still active for restricted rooms.
The shift handover does not identify the overdue badges or assign follow-up.
anomalies.inspectionDetails:
RECORD EVIDENCE
Two sampled visitor entries have departure times on the previous shift but no badge return confirmation.
The linked badge records remain enabled and have no expiration time. Their access groups include the equipment room, which was not authorized for either visit.
The site's visitor procedure requires sponsor approval, limited area access, and deactivation at visit end.

DESK OBSERVATIONS
The workstation is locked when unattended and blank cards are secured; these passing controls do not address the active badge permissions.
The handover has no exception entry or assigned owner for the two unreturned badges.
A designated historical record was inspected; no attempt was made to use an actual visitor credential.
The evidence establishes excessive ongoing authorization, not actual unauthorized entry.
anomalies.nistControl:
PE-2 Physical Access Authorizations; PE-3 Physical Access Control
PE-8 Visitor Access Records; AC-2 Account Management
anomalies.riskGuidance:
Consider misuse of a lost or retained badge and the exposure of rooms outside the approved visit scope.
Check deactivation, access-group correction, and review of relevant entry events as separate follow-up actions.

information.status:
The network console is locked when unattended, and management access uses a named account through the approved bastion.
The current configuration backup and a sampled alert acknowledgement are recorded.
information.inspectionDetails:
PHYSICAL CHECK
The console is in the restricted network area. No password note, unattended console cable, or unrecorded USB device is visible.
Patch-panel labels match the sampled port assignments in the network diagram.

MANAGEMENT EVIDENCE
The sampled switch management address exposes TCP 22 for SSH and TCP 443 for HTTPS only to the management bastion. The monitoring collector alone is permitted UDP 161 using SNMPv3 with authentication/privacy.
Service identification comes from the switch configuration export, not a desktop process listing. Telnet and HTTP management are disabled.
The operator uses a named administrative identity; emergency device access is vaulted and audited.
The latest configuration backup completed, and a separate sampled restore-validation record is present.
A current link-fault test generated the expected alert and acknowledgement; the test port was restored.
The management restriction was corroborated by a denied connection test from the user VLAN.
information.nistControl:
AC-11 Device Lock; AC-17 Remote Access
CM-6 Configuration Settings; SC-7 Boundary Protection
CP-9 System Backup; SI-4 System Monitoring
information.riskGuidance:
Consider whether access to the console permits changes across many network devices.
Evaluate physical access, administrative identity, management isolation, and configuration recovery together.

information.status:
The console's monitoring view is read-only under the current operator role.
Recent network changes are linked to approvals, and the sampled running configuration matches the approved change record.
information.inspectionDetails:
OBSERVATIONS
The operator's normal monitoring role cannot save device configuration. Privileged changes require a separately authorized session.
The unattended console locks under the local policy, and no console session is left authenticated on a connected device.

RECORD SAMPLE
A sampled VLAN change has an approved purpose, affected interfaces, implementation record, and post-change connectivity checks.
The current configuration export matches the recorded change, including separation of user, server, and out-of-band management networks.
The inventory identifies the sampled switch and its support owner.
Configuration backups and central change/audit logs have recent successful collection records.
The timestamp on the network event sample agrees with the logging platform within local tolerance.
A successful sample is not a substitute for reviewing every switch or every VLAN rule.
information.nistControl:
AC-6 Least Privilege; CM-3 Configuration Change Control
CM-8 System Component Inventory; AU-8 Time Stamps
AU-12 Audit Record Generation
information.riskGuidance:
Assess accidental or unauthorized network-wide changes and whether they can be reconstructed and reversed.
A read-only dashboard is a useful separation of duties only if elevated sessions and device credentials are also controlled.

anomalies.status:
An unattended network-console session has full device-configuration privileges under a shared account.
The sampled switch permits Telnet management from the user network, outside the approved bastion path.
anomalies.inspectionDetails:
CONSOLE OBSERVATIONS
The screen remains unlocked with an active privileged device session. No operator is present and the local device-lock policy is disabled.
A console lead is connected to the sampled switch, and the current session can enter configuration mode. The assessor makes no changes.

DEVICE CONFIGURATION EVIDENCE
TCP 23 is enabled for Telnet management; TCP 22 for SSH and TCP 443 for HTTPS are also enabled. Device configuration identifies these services.
An approved connectivity test from the user VLAN reaches the Telnet listener. No credentials are submitted over that connection.
The management ACL allows the user subnet, contrary to the management-only baseline.
Recent configuration entries identify the same shared administrator account for multiple operators.
No approved exception covers either the console exposure or Telnet use.
anomalies.nistControl:
AC-11 Device Lock; AC-2 Account Management; AC-17 Remote Access
CM-6 Configuration Settings; SC-7 Boundary Protection
anomalies.riskGuidance:
Consider broad configuration impact, interception risk from unprotected legacy management, and weak accountability.
The confirmed defect is an exposed, unapproved management path and unattended privilege; it does not establish that a device has been compromised.

anomalies.status:
The console shows successful monitoring, but configuration backups for the sampled switches have failed repeatedly.
A recent production VLAN change has no approved change record or recoverable matching configuration snapshot.
anomalies.inspectionDetails:
RECORD EVIDENCE
The configuration-backup job history shows seven consecutive daily authentication failures for the sampled devices.
The dashboard's green availability icon reflects ping responses, not backup success.
The latest available configuration snapshot predates a production VLAN change recorded in the device audit log.
No corresponding approved change ticket or post-change validation is found in the operations register.

CORROBORATING CHECKS
The backup failure alerts are unacknowledged, and the shift handover has no recovery owner assigned.
The operator session is individually authenticated and the console locks correctly; these do not close the change-control and recoverability gaps.
No restore or rollback was attempted against live equipment during the assessment.
The absence of a current snapshot does not prove an outage will occur, but it weakens recovery and reliable reconstruction of changes.
anomalies.nistControl:
CP-9 System Backup; CP-10 System Recovery and Reconstitution
CM-3 Configuration Change Control; AU-6 Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
anomalies.riskGuidance:
Assess prolonged recovery and loss of confidence in the approved network state after a failure or unintended change.
Verify backup content and restoration evidence rather than treating device reachability or a green overview icon as proof of recoverability.
